messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah@novahealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP checkpoint: throughput delta and ask for weekly review

Connor —

Thanks for the last sync. We ran a short production-ish run over the weekend (300k inference tokens across mixed-length requests) and I wanted to surface early numbers ahead of next week's MAP checkpoint. Key bullets: 
- Observed P50 latencies ~45ms, P95 ~125ms (seq len 256) on the current redwood-medium deployment.
- Throughput peaked at ~230 req/s, but we see intermittent 10–20% dips under bursty traffic.
- Our infra team (procurement in copy) is pressing for a clear tuning plan and timeline tied to the MAP so we can lock the committed SLAs.

Can we run through the performance gate metrics at the weekly checkpoint on 6/20? Would appreciate a snapshot of tuning options and owners so we can commit dates to procurement.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Director, Platform Integrations
NovaHealth

Attachments: perf_report_weekend_excerpt.csv (high-level summary)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint: throughput delta and ask for weekly review

Sarah —

Thanks for the data and the heads-up. Draft agenda for the 6/20 MAP checkpoint below: 
1) Quick sync on NovaHealth traffic profile and weekend numbers (Sarah) — 5m
2) Redwood benchmarking readout (Marissa) — 15m
3) Shortlist of tunables (batching, KV/prefix cache, quantization variant, kernel selection) — 10m
4) Action register: owners, smoke tests, MAP timeline updates — 10m

Preliminary notes from our side: 
- We ran microbenchmarks that mirror your traffic (mixed short/medium seq lengths). Baseline (no KV cache) P50=42ms, P95=120ms. Enabling KV prefix caching brought throughput from ~225 req/s to ~315 req/s under the same load profile in lab.
- We suspect two main contributors to the observed in-prod dips: (1) a suboptimal kernel path for longer sequences on the current GPU family and (2) autoscaler thresholds that are too conservative for burst windows.

I asked Marissa to prepare a short CSV with p50/p95 across seq lengths (64/128/256) plus a quick table of recommended tuning steps with estimated impact and risk. Karthik will bring proposed autoscale threshold changes.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: 6/20 MAP checkpoint — benchmarking readout & actions (notes)

Team, Sarah —

Notes from today's MAP checkpoint (performance benchmarking focus). I included the lab CSV as perf_report_0620.csv. Summary first, then the action register.

Executive summary:
- Lab summary (mixed workload, 1k req steady run, spike windows modeled at +60%):
  - Seq len 64: P50 18ms, P95 48ms, throughput 410 req/s
  - Seq len 128: P50 32ms, P95 86ms, throughput 370 req/s
  - Seq len 256: P50 42ms, P95 120ms, baseline throughput 225 req/s; with KV prefix cache enabled throughput jumped to 320 req/s; tail improved by ~15%.
- Root causes: kernel selection for longer sequences yields unnecessary memory copies; autoscaler cooldowns keep us below ideal concurrency during burst windows.

Tuning recommendations (ranked):
A) Enable KV prefix caching for NovaHealth production bucket (low risk) — expected +35–45% throughput for mixed workloads.
B) Adopt fused attention kernel on the redwood-medium model (requires small model recompile & smoke test) — expected P95 reduction 8–12% for seq >=128.
C) Trial 4-bit quantized variant (redwood-medium-4q) for a portion of traffic — risk: slight quality degradation on edge prompts; expected cost reduction ~30% and throughput boost ~20%.
D) Autoscaling tuning: lower scale-up threshold, shorten cooldown during business hours — expected to reduce burst misses.

Action register (owners & dates):
- Marissa Cole — run fused-attention compile + smoke test on staging (target: 2k step smoke; validate P95 impact) — due 2028-06-24 — attachment: kernel_selection_notes.txt
- Karthik Iyer — propose autoscaler policy delta (scale-up threshold, cooldown window) and updated policy JSON for Prod test — due 2028-06-27
- Monica Patel — update MAP timeline PDF to reflect new tuning commitments and procurement checkpoints; coordinate with NovaHealth procurement for SLA lock dates — due 2028-06-25
- Connor O'Brien — produce a single-page MAP change log and a short note tying tuning items to committed MAP milestones for procurement — due 2028-06-22

Risks & mitigation:
- Quantization (4q) requires prompt-set regression checks. Marissa will include a small prompt-set eval in smoke test.
- Kernel compile needs a fallback plan; we will stage rollout to canary VMs and watch P95 for 24h before broader roll.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Perf & Eval Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: perf_report_0620.csv, kernel_selection_notes.txt
